features.title: Install the Web UI as an app on the phone
features.summary: The Host serves its own manifest with PNG icons (any and maskable) and a splash color, and injects the head tags Safari on iOS needs for a standalone home-screen launch with its own icon instead of a page screenshot. Registered on the Host Web server, so the Tailscale tunnel, the LAN listener and the desktop URL all get it. No service worker: Chrome has not required one for installation since 108, and a cache in front of a live agent client only risks stale code.
features.currentSurface: host: served manifest, icon routes and index head

configuration.constraints: Non-empty manifest name shown by the browser and the OS app list.
Home-screen label; iOS truncates what does not fit.
CSS color painted behind the icon while the installed app boots.

failureModes: A request for an icon the generator did not produce answers 404 and never reads another file.
A non-read method on the manifest or an icon answers 405 instead of serving bytes.
Without this plugin the shell still installs on Chrome; only the iOS standalone launch, the touch icon and the splash color are missing.

verification.testName: keeps the shell metadata the stock manifest declares
offers the raster sizes an Android launcher and maskable icon require
uses the configured branding for the installed app name and splash
declares the touch icon, standalone mode, label and status bar style
escapes a configured label instead of ending the attribute
adds the tags inside the head, before anything the app renders
every icon the manifest advertises exists as a PNG of its declared size
serves a known icon as a cacheable PNG at the exact bounds

verification.reason: The bundle registers Host Web server routes and one index transform, so it adds no client surface to walk: the served manifest, icons and head are proven by the unit tests and a Chromium installability probe, and the app it decorates is already covered by every other bundle's journeys.

telemetry.reason: The plugin registers two Web server routes and one index tap; the Web server owns the socket and this code fetches, spawns and schedules nothing.
